# DMAS.JK — industrial-estate land bank, killed on price, revisited 9% cheaper

Signal / why now: NEGLECTED #3 / MOMENTUM #2 at Rp167, −9.2% below the 2026-10-12 kill at 184 and 22% off the 214 high, with the 30-day cooldown expiring today. The 2026-11-08 9M print shows H1-2026 NI Rp1,192bn vs Rp433bn, and a Rp1.4trn interim dividend (Rp29/sh, 17% of price) was declared 10-29.

Regime AGAINST — variant: the desk's AVOID is a funding-leg/mortgage-affordability call; DMAS is debt-free with Rp2.1tn net cash and sells industrial-estate land (Kota Deltamas/Greenland) to industrial and data-centre tenants on a USD-linked cycle, so neither the funding leg nor mortgage rates reach its P&L.

Archetype: property_nav_discount_narrowing · method PROPERTY_NAV_DISCOUNT (1.15x book — the discount is to industrial-land RNAV, not to book; flag for the analyst).

Three questions: (1) Does the 9M filing confirm H1 was recurring land sales, or a one-off block sale? The export has no Q3 row, so H1→9M must be read from the filing. (2) What repeatable FY27 land-sale volume remains once the data-centre buyers have taken their tranche? (3) Is the Rp1.4trn interim covered by cash, not presale receipts already spent?

Fast-disqualify: registry EV 0.38×+45 + 0.62×−25 = +1.6% over 2.5y, capital-only and thin — but the cash leg (9.9% trailing, 17% interim) makes total EV positive ✓. Valuation anchor: 6.5x FY26E EPS ~Rp37 = Rp240 (+44%), clearing the +45% up-leg ✓; downside to book Rp145 (−13%). Sources: IDX 9M-2026 filing + FY25 AR, both reachable ✓.

Displaces BBYB under the ≤12 active cap.
